Excellent thermal stability was achieved due to the impediment of the grain growth by the secondary particles.

the main strengthening mechanism found in the MA + SPS equiatomic CoCrFeNiNb alloy can be attributed to grain boundary strengthening, solid solution strengthening (due to the presence of considerably larger Nb atoms compared to the rest of elements) and strengthening by a high volume fraction of homogeneously dispersed Laves phases.

Nevertheless, this strengthening contribution is minimal when comparing the overall compression yield stress, which in the present case was experimentally evaluated to be sy y 2300 MPa. This would actually possibly account for 1 e2% and thence fits well within the experimental errors.
The dislocation strengthening calculated by Eq. (3) was sd ¼ 310 ± 20 MPa.
Considering this value, the Hall-Petch strengthening contribution yield by the g-phase was calculated as sHP ¼ 940 ± 50 MPa.
The mean twin strengthening contribution was thus sTB ¼ 340 ± 40 MPa.
Thus, the secondary phase particle strengthening contribution was calculated as Dsspp ¼ 570 ± 110 MPa.

Thence, the Laves load transfer strengthening contribution accounted for sLT Laves ¼ 285 ± 10 MPa, while the corresponding strengthening contribution from the Cr 2O3 was sLT Cr2O3 ¼ 4 ± 1 MPa and thus negligible.
Therefore, according to Eqs. (8a) and (8b), the two thermal expansion strengthening terms were sTE Cr2O3 ¼ 280 ± 60 MPa and sTE Laves ¼ 330 ± 60 MPa.
That is, the Orowan strengthening did not occur in the present case.
